intent_snapshot.goal: Align leader resolve with ULS: resume applies only to WorkItem escalated without a batch blocker while needs_human batches and lane_executor_no_progress children admit only ask_owner (the recorded amendment of loop-leader D4 and S4-AC1); a Lane dialog is asked once by planEscalation and a leader ask_owner on it annotates in place; lane_session_unavailable never counts as a refusal or replan round nor changes the briefing fingerprint and shows as environment_blocked in status; batch lookup uses findActiveLaneBatchForTask and briefing batches carry v3 session facts, per D5 of docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-DEC-A2, BR-REQ-A1; meet D5.1 and D5.4 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-replan.test.ts, tests/loop-leader-briefing.test.ts. Done looks like: resume on an escalated item with no batch blocker is accepted; briefing batches carry each child's session generation, no_progress and attention. Negative: resume on a needs_human batch or a lane_executor_no_progress child is rejected and only ask_owner is accepted; two active batch records for one task make the batch lookup refuse instead of taking the first file.

Source BR-DEC-A3, BR-SCN-A2; meet D5.2 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-replan.test.ts, tests/loop-sched-interaction-github.test.ts. Done looks like: a child blocked on a startup dialog yields exactly one lane_entry_blocked comment on the Issue and appears in the briefing as a pending interaction. Negative: a leader ask_owner on the same subject annotates that request in place and posts no second comment.

Source BR-DEC-A6, BR-SCN-A4; meet D5.3 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-briefing.test.ts, tests/loop-leader-replan.test.ts. Done looks like: five ticks refused lane_session_unavailable leave refused_transitions, replan_rounds, the briefing fingerprint and the leader wake count unchanged, and imm-loop status --json shows environment_blocked lane_session_unavailable on the item. Negative: a different refusal reason still counts toward the three-refusal trigger.

intent_snapshot.scope_size_reason: The resume rule, the single-question rule and the refusal exclusion all change what the leader may do with a blocked batch and share the briefing and replan code; together they are one resolve contract.

attestations.summary: S5-AC1..3 met: resume gated on needs_human/no_progress blockers with batch lookup via findActiveLaneBatchForTask (ambiguity throws, dispatch rejects as resolve_facts_unavailable), briefing children carry generation/no_progress/attention, labelled lane_entry_blocked escalation annotated in place and listed as pending interaction, lane_session_unavailable kept out of refusals/revision/fingerprint and surfaced as environment_blocked_items; antigravity mirror byte-identical; blast radius medium (loop_daemon replan/leader_agent/cli, optional WorkItem.environment_blocked persisted field).

advisory_findings.summary: isChildHeldForOwner treats every needs_human child (e.g. lane_executor_no_progress) as held, so an already-answered lane_entry_blocked comment stays pending and listed in the briefing while that child is parked for an unrelated reason.

evidence.trigger: lane_entry_blocked comment on Issue 42 whose dialog was answered, then the same child parked needs_human with reason lane_executor_no_progress → pending_lane_entry_blocked non-empty and a lane-entry-blocked interaction still in the briefing

findings.summary: A lane_entry_blocked escalation comment is never withdrawn, so pendingLaneEntryBlocked treats an already-answered Lane dialog as pending forever: resume, release and replan on that Issue are refused permanently, and a later ask_owner annotates the stale dialog comment instead of asking the new question.

evidence.trigger: Issue 42 gets a lane_entry_blocked escalation comment (agent_handlers escalateOnce, label lane_entry_blocked). The owner answers the dialog in Herdr and the Lane continues; the batch child is no longer blocked, but nothing in escalation.ts, agent_handlers.ts or cli.ts withdraws the comment. Later the item escalates for another reason with no batch blocker. collectResolveFacts -> pendingLaneEntryBlocked still returns escalation:lane_entry_blocked:<key> from the observed comments, so resolveBlockers adds pending_lane_entry_blocked and resume is rejected (the S5-AC1 Done case says resume should be accepted), and askOwnerQuestion picks deps.pending_lane_entry_blocked[0] and annotates the old dialog comment with unrelated context. The briefing reads blocked state from the live batch child, so it disagrees with the resolve facts. Fix: derive the pending dialog from the live v3 child state (or withdraw the comment once the child leaves the blocked or unsubmitted state), and add a test where an answered dialog's comment no longer blocks resume.

findings.summary: No test covers the S5-AC2 Done clause 'appears in the briefing as a pending interaction': readBatchSummaries' blocked_children path and the lane_entry_blocked interaction it adds to collectLeaderBriefingInput are never exercised. The predicate also flags every enrolled child whose entry is not yet submitted, not only a child blocked on a dialog.

evidence.trigger: A v3 batch child in state enrolled with session.attention 'blocked' is bound to a work item, and collectLeaderBriefingInput runs. No test in tests/loop-leader-briefing.test.ts, tests/loop-leader-replan.test.ts or tests/loop-sched-interaction-github.test.ts asserts an interaction of kind lane_entry_blocked in the briefing; the only briefing seed uses entry_submitted true and attention stalled. So a regression that drops or mislabels the interaction passes QA. Separately, a healthy child that is still starting (entry_submitted false, no dialog) is reported as a pending owner question and changes the fingerprint. Fix: add a briefing test for a dialog-blocked child, a negative test for a normally starting child, and narrow the predicate to the dialog state.
